overlap_rationale: Both Study A (Ducrot 2017, Physics and Chemistry of the Earth) and Study B (Ducrot & Bourblanc 2017, Natural Resources Forum) are distinct companion journal articles analyzing the exact same three-stage empirical study of the pilot PRONASAR rural water supply programme (2011-2013) in Mabalane district, Gaza Province, semi-arid Mozambique. Both papers rely on: (1) institutional document review and key informant interviews with national, provincial, district and NGO actors conducted in 2012-2013; (2) qualitative fieldwork in the exact same 12 villages across Mabalane's three water-access zones (leader interviews, water committee focus groups, infrastructure walks and women's focus groups in two villages); and (3) the exact same wealth-stratified household survey (N = 119 interviews, sampling 20% of households across four leader-classified wealth groups) in three riverine villages, including the same 18-option card preference exercise (e.g. 39% rejecting small reservoir rehabilitation in both papers, matching village household count discrepancies such as the 69-household village, and matching water-fee timeliness and saline borehole vs river reliance by wealth group). Whereas Study A focuses on village-level water committee functioning, leadership and institutional bricolage, Study B analyzes distributive, procedural and contextual equity across district planning, contractor drilling allocation and community maintenance.
study_a_sample_and_data: Mabalane district, Gaza Province, Mozambique (Limpopo Basin), evaluating the PRONASAR pilot programme (2011-2013; fieldwork/fee records from 2012-2013 under the CPWF Limpopo Basin Development Challenge). Three-step mixed-methods dataset: (1) programme document review and interviews with national, provincial and district actors; (2) qualitative village-level survey in 12 communities across three water-access zones (village leader interviews, water committee focus groups, transect walks to water structures, and women's focus groups in 2 villages); and (3) stratified random household survey of N = 119 respondents (20% per wealth quartile across 4 leader-ranked wealth groups) in 3 riverine villages (36, 66 and 16 interviews; plus 2012 fee ledger records for 275 registered households in Village 1 and an 18-option card preference exercise).
study_b_sample_and_data: Mabalane district, Gaza Province, Mozambique (Limpopo Basin), evaluating the PRONASAR pilot programme (fieldwork in second half of 2012 and post-2013 flood follow-up, triangulated with 2012 UEM water-point mapping across 64 district villages). Same three-step mixed-methods dataset: (1) institutional/document analysis and interviews with national, provincial, district and NGO actors; (2) qualitative village-level survey in the same 12 communities (18.4% of district villages) across the seven localities and three water-access zones (leader interviews, water-point manager/committee focus groups, infrastructure walks, and women's focus groups in 2 villages); and (3) the same stratified household survey of n = 119 families (20% sampled from 4 leader-defined wealth groups) in 3 riverine communities, including the 18-option preference exercise and water-fee/source questions.
